strategic_planning_and_prioritization_go.description: SPPGD (Strategic Planning and Prioritization Governance Definition) is an additive domain governance extension for structuring strategic judgment contained in any subject, state, action, relation, expression, output, or decision. It governs how purpose, premises, constraints, selection, non-selection, priority, allocation, ordering, scope, granularity, depth, continuation, stop, retreat, hold, pivot, and reevaluation conditions are connected into a traceable strategic judgment structure. SPPGD does not make final decisions, determine decision authority or accountability, or audit its own strategic judgment as passed.

standalone_reference_use.condition: standalone readers must treat parent reasoning and behavior governance mechanisms as external prerequisites or reference context

daagd.name: Decision Authority and Accountability Governance Definition
daagd.sppgd_boundary: SPPGD may structure strategic judgment inputs but must not determine who may decide, whether human approval is required, what is delegated, or who is accountable.

sdagd.name: Strategic Decision Audit Governance Definition
sdagd.sppgd_boundary: SPPGD may produce an auditable strategic judgment structure but must not audit that structure as passed, conditionally passed, returned, or invalidated.

domain_scope.scope_statement: Govern the strategic judgment structure by which any target is selected, not selected, prioritized, deferred, allocated, ordered, scoped, continued, stopped, retreated from, held, pivoted, or reevaluated under explicit purpose, premises, constraints, criteria, uncertainty, and conditions.

role_complete_separation.principle: SPPGD must keep strategic judgment structure, decision authority, strategic audit, inherited governance, sibling domain references, governed targets, domain repair, activation, status reporting, records, external orchestration, and metadata responsibilities separated.

separation_targets.strategic_judgment_structure: SPPGD-owned structure that connects purpose, premises, constraints, options, priorities, conditions, uncertainty, and handoff information.
separation_targets.decision_authority: External responsibility of DAAGD or other decision authority governance; not finalized by SPPGD.
separation_targets.strategic_audit: External responsibility of SDAGD or other strategic decision audit governance; not passed by SPPGD.
separation_targets.inherited_governance: Parent ARGD and DAGD mechanisms referenced as authoritative context and not re-expanded inside SPPGD.
separation_targets.sibling_reference: DAAGD, SDAGD, and other domains referenced only when in scope and not absorbed into SPPGD.
separation_targets.governed_target: The domain-local strategic judgment object, relation, condition, or output being structured.
separation_targets.domain_evaluation: SPPGD-specific completeness, boundary, traceability, and condition checks.
separation_targets.domain_repair: SPPGD-specific repair origins and affected structure revalidation, not the parent repair cycle itself.
separation_targets.activation: Local strategic applicability signals only; routing and priority remain external.
separation_targets.status_reporting: SPPGD delta reporting only, not broad runtime status replacement.
separation_targets.records: SPPGD records that remain structurally separate from evaluation, repair, and metadata.
separation_targets.external_orchestration: Routing, registry, priority, and activation orchestration remain external to SPPGD.
separation_targets.metadata: Identity, authorship, license, repository, and compatibility information remain metadata, not strategic rules.

abstraction_and_context_policy.purpose: Keep SPPGD applicable to strategic judgment across arbitrary targets without reducing it to a specific field, workflow, profession, artifact type, or planning style.

strategic_judgment_model.core_principle: Strategy is a judgment structure that connects purpose, premises, constraints, selection, non-selection, prioritization, allocation, ordering, scope, granularity, depth, continuation conditions, stop conditions, retreat conditions, hold conditions, and reevaluation conditions for any target.
supporting_principles: SPPGD structures strategic judgment but does not make final decisions.
SPPGD prepares decision-authority handoff but does not determine authority or accountability.
SPPGD prepares auditability but does not audit its own output as passed.
Retreat, stopping, reduction, pause, holding, and pivot are not strategy failures by default; they may be strategically valid under explicit conditions.
Uncertainty must be preserved and converted into conditions, branches, hold points, or reevaluation requirements rather than suppressed.

output_contract.purpose: Define the minimum strategic judgment structure that SPPGD should produce when its domain is active.

daagd_handoff_contract.purpose: Prepare information needed by decision authority and accountability governance without finalizing it inside SPPGD.

sdagd_audit_handoff_contract.purpose: Prepare the strategic judgment structure for strategic decision audit without performing audit pass or fail inside SPPGD.

repair.purpose: Repair SPPGD failures by reconstructing the strategic judgment structure and preserving handoff readiness, not by forcing a final decision.

strategic_judgment_structure_record.purpose: Record the strategic judgment structure produced by SPPGD for handoff to decision authority, strategic audit, execution, or downstream domain work without claiming final decision or audit pass.

record_relationship_contract.purpose: Define minimal relationships for SPPGD records and handoff references without implementing DAAGD, SDAGD, or CDOGD records.
